title: Evidence for Chapter 26: war finance, reparations, the hyperinflation and the stabilization of 1923-1924
source: Keynes (1919, 1923, 1925, 1929) and the rejoinder; Ohlin (1929); Bresciani-Turroni (1937); Sargent (1982); Fischer, Sahay and Végh (2002); Koech (2011); Fisher (1930); the Rentenbank decree (1923); the London Schedule (1921); the Bundesarchiv; the Neue Deutsche Biographie; NobelPrize.org; Wikisource
series: Evidence rows: id, place, year, values (';' separated, in the order of the quotation), unit, source key, page or section, the source text verbatim, note
license: Quotations for criticism, scholarship and teaching, each with its source; no full original is redistributed. Keynes (1883-1946): the works of 1919, 1923, 1925 and 1929 are in the public domain in the United Kingdom (life plus 70 years); the Project Gutenberg text is used under the Project Gutenberg licence (no Project Gutenberg trademark is used here). Bresciani-Turroni (1937, 'ALL RIGHTS RESERVED'), Ohlin (1929; Ohlin died in 1979) and the Neue Deutsche Biographie (1969-2005) are in copyright: short phrases only, the rest paraphrased. Sargent (1982), in the NBER volume: '© 1982 by The National Bureau of Economic Research. All rights reserved.' (row s_copyright); short passages only, with full credit to the author, the volume and the NBER. Fischer, Sahay and Végh (2002): '© 2002 by Stanley Fischer, Ratna Sahay and Carlos A. Végh. All rights reserved. Short sections of text, not to exceed two paragraphs, may be quoted without explicit permission provided that full credit, including © notice, is given to the source.' (row fsv_notice). Koech (2011), Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas: 'Articles may be reprinted on the condition that the source is credited and a copy is provided to the Globalization and Monetary Policy Institute' (row ko_terms). Fisher (1930), Econlib edition: 'The text of this edition is in the public domain'. The Rentenbank decree and the London Schedule are official documents in the public domain; the Wikisource transcription is CC BY-SA. The Bundesarchiv pages and NobelPrize.org are cited for facts. Data transcriptions are factual subsets. The chapter's Chinese renders the quotations; the translations are the book's.
notes: Every quotation is checked word for word against the cached source text by data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py, and every value is read from its quotation by checks/check_ch26.py. The words of Helfferich, Havenstein and Luther are indirect testimony (through Bresciani-Turroni's English edition); the Cologne rates come from Schacht (1926) through Bresciani-Turroni; Cagan's definition and dates come through Fischer, Sahay and Végh; the price, budget and dismissal figures come through Sargent from Young (1925), which was not obtained, nor was the Statistisches Reichsamt's Zahlen zur Geldentwertung (1925). British number words in Bresciani-Turroni: milliard = 10^9, billion = 10^12, trillion = 10^18. OCR errors are kept in the quotations and read in the notes.
